injury.comment: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
Adam Schefter of ESPN reported on Sunday NFL Countdown that "there is not a lot of optimism" that Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) will suit up Sunday at Denver, but the tight end is "pushing to play."
Cunningham (knee) is probable to play Sunday in Atlanta.
Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports.

injury.comment: Maye, who reportedly suffered a fractured right fibula last Sunday, is on track to miss at least six weeks, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network.
Harper (hip) is expected to miss two to three weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
Antetokounmpo (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Oklahoma City, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.

Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports.
Holliday will undergo left wrist surgery next week, Jake Rill of MLB.com reports.

Hurts (calf) is expected to be held out of football activities for multiple months and miss the rest of the season after new imaging over the weekend revealed several blood clots in his lungs, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.

Hill's (knee) agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Tuesday that the receiver hasn't yet been medically cleared but is expected to be "in a few weeks," James Palmer of Bleacher Report reports.
